newsitem.title: USA: Pilot board vote on American offer not seen today.
newsitem.headline: Pilot board vote on American offer not seen today.

text.p: The board of the Allied Pilots Association was not expected to vote on the proposed contract agreement with AMR Corp unit American Airlines until Saturday, union spokesman Wally Pitts said on Friday.
"We do not expect any decision on the agreement in principle today," Pitts told reporters.
Pitts said the negotiating committee would brief the board until noon today (1700 GMT) and then the board would adjourn until tomorrow.
During the rest of the day the negotiating committee would be putting the agreement in principle into contractual terms, a step needed before the board could take a vote.
Pitts emphasized that the question of whether Allied Pilots Association members would fly regional jets remained a key issue, although he declined to give any details.
"We're concerned American will expand the regional fleet and shrink the American fleet," he said.
